text: Castlebridge (Irish: Droichead an Chaisleáin) is a small town in County Wexford, Ireland, located approximately 5 km north of Wexford town and just north of Wexford Harbour on the R741 road. It has become a rapidly expanding suburb of Wexford Town, with its population increasing from 783 in 1996 to 1,840 in 2016—a rise of nearly threefold over 20 years.[1][3] The original castle in the town was dismantled to construct buildings, including the Church of Ireland church, one of the oldest structures in Castlebridge. The river flowing through the town is actually a canal that replaced the original river; it was dug by hand to enable sailing cots loaded at Castlebridge’s docks to reach Wexford Town more efficiently.[citation needed] Fr James Dixon, the first Catholic priest allowed to minister in Australia, was born in Castlebridge in 1758.[4] Castlebridge is also the founding place of the Guinness Book of World Records. On 10 November 1951, Sir Hugh Beaver, then managing director of the Guinness Breweries, participated in a shooting party in the North Slob near the River Slaney in County Wexford, where he became involved in a debate over whether the golden plover or the red grouse was Europe’s fastest game bird (the golden plover being correct).[6] That evening at Castlebridge House, he realized that existing reference books did not provide answers to such questions, and he recognized that a book offering definitive answers to common pub debates could be popular.[7][8][9] In 2019, Diageo and the Pattison Group, who hold the rights to the Guinness Book of Records, expressed strong interest in Castlebridge House, which has remained derelict, with feasibility studies now underway by Wexford County Council to assess the damage and plan for its restoration, with the goal of developing it into a tourist attraction linked to the book’s origins.[10] This interest was highlighted by the launch of the first annual Castlebridge Record Makers Family Fun Festival in 2019, featuring exhibits on the book’s history and significance to the town.[11] Wexford Bus operates an hourly service, route 877 "The Bridge Loop," to and from Wexford on Mondays and Saturdays since February 2019.[12] Bus Éireann route 379 (Wexford–Gorey via Kilmuckridge and Courtown) serves Castlebridge on Mondays and Saturdays. The town’s center includes a 60x30 foot handball alley, where the handball club has produced several county and Irish champions and members have competed at World Championships in the United States.[citation needed] Nearby, opposite the Old School (now the Castlebridge Community Centre), is the local soccer club, Bridge Rovers FC.[citation needed] Patrick Breen, who lived in Castlebridge and was originally from Bannow in southern County Wexford, was the first Wexford person to serve as President of the Gaelic Athletic Association from 1924 to 1926—among only two Wexford individuals to hold the position.[13] He also founded the Irish Handball Council and the past pupils union of St. Peters College and is buried in the Castlebridge cemetery.[citation needed] Community groups in the area include the Castlebridge Gospel Choir, founded in 2003. Local businesses include the Porter House, which was named 'Pub of the Year' in 2017 before closing, along with several fast food restaurants, a local Londis supermarket, a furniture shop, an antiques store, and a post office.
